t: Arabic, first recorded in inscriptions of the Arabian peninsula and its desert borderlands, became a world language with the Qur’an and the Islamic conquests of the 7th century.

As the language of the caliphates it carried philosophy, science, medicine and mathematics, translated from Greek, Persian and Sanskrit and developed by scholars from Spain to Central Asia, and its literature is one of the richest in the world.

Today spoken by some 400 million people in a family of varieties, with a shared standard written language, it is the language of prayer for Muslims everywhere and has lent words from algebra to coffee to the languages of the world.
dyk: English words such as algebra, alcohol, sugar, coffee, cotton and zero come from Arabic, and algorithm comes from the name of the 9th-century Baghdad mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
ev: An Assyrian inscription names “Gindibu the Arab” among the enemies of Shalmaneser III, the first known mention of Arabs
The Namara inscription, the epitaph of Imru' al-Qays, “king of all the Arabs”, is carved in Arabic in Nabataean letters
The Zabad inscription, in Greek, Syriac and Arabic, is one of the oldest dated texts in the Arabic script
The Qur’an is revealed to Muhammad, according to Muslim belief, and becomes the first book in Arabic
The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik makes Arabic the language of government
Sibawayh writes the first comprehensive grammar of Arabic
Al-Khwarizmi writes his book on algebra in Baghdad
Arabic becomes an official language of the United Nations

f.family: Afroasiatic: the Central Semitic branch of the Semitic languages
f.script: The Arabic alphabet, developed from the Nabataean form of the Aramaic script and written from right to left
f.earliest: Inscriptions of the Syro-Arabian desert from around the 1st century BCE, regarded by many scholars as Old Arabic; the Namara inscription of 328 CE
f.status: The first language of some 400 million people in many varieties; the liturgical language of Islam; official in more than twenty countries and at the United Nations
